posts.title: Sunnyside flood barrier is finished

slides.headline: Sunnyside's flood barrier is finished.
details: 2.4 km along the Bow, built for a one-in-100-year flood.
13 years after the 2013 flood.
slides.footer: Source: City of Calgary, Calgary Herald

slides.headline: $73 million, 200 new trees.
details: It has been working since May and protects Sunnyside and Hillhurst.
Some pathway and road closures stay until landscaping wraps up at the end of October.

posts.caption:
Sunnyside's flood barrier is officially finished, 13 years after the 2013 flood.

It runs 2.4 km along the Bow, is built for a one-in-100-year flood, and has been protecting Sunnyside and Hillhurst since May. The project cost $73 million and added about 200 trees. A few pathway and road closures stay until the landscaping is done at the end of October.

Sources: City of Calgary, Calgary Herald.

posts.title: Last home opener at the Saddledome

slides.headline: The last home opener at the 'Dome.
details: Thursday, Oct. 1: Flames vs. Seattle Kraken.
The Saddledome opened in 1983. This is its farewell season.

posts.caption:
Thursday is the last home opener the Saddledome will ever host.

The Flames start the 2026–27 regular season at home against the Seattle Kraken on Oct. 1. The 'Dome opened in 1983, and this is its farewell season before the team moves to Scotia Place.

First game you saw there?

Source: Calgary Flames.

posts.title: What's on the Oct. 19 referendum ballot

slides.headline: 10 questions on your referendum ballot.
details: Here's what each one asks, in plain words.
Swipe →

slides.headline: Immigration and services
details: 1. More provincial control of immigration, to under 1% of the population (about 50,000 a year).
2. Provincial programs only for citizens, permanent residents and Alberta-approved immigrants.
3. A 12-month wait for non-permanent residents before social supports.
4. Health and education fees for non-permanent residents.

slides.headline: Voting, courts and Ottawa
details: 5. Proof of citizenship to vote.
6. Provinces, not Ottawa, pick provincial court judges.
7. Pursue abolishing the Senate.
8. Opt out of federal programs and keep the funding.
9. Provincial law wins over federal law in shared areas.

slides.headline: Stay, or hold a separation vote
details: Whether Alberta stays a province of Canada or moves to a binding referendum on separating.
Voting day is Monday, Oct. 19.

posts.caption:
